page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware support. The server includes 322 GB of bundled local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reflect consistent mid-tier results across compute and data-processing tasks. Under stress-ng, the instance achieves 1898.99 for single-core and 7760.14 for multi-core performance. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1637.0 and a multi-core score of 6053.0, with clang software compilation scoring 8163.0. The memory subsystem delivers 417.12 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 58.17 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, while write operations sustain 42.04 GB/sec. Redis caching demonstrates 8.01 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 12.1 GB/sec. A notable tradeoff appears in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which scores 31.99 GB/sec in the lower quartile of tested systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced core-to-memory allocation and direct inclusion of 322 GB local SSD storage eliminate the immediate requirement for external storage attachments in temporary data workloads. The resource profile fits general-purpose production workloads, including relational database engines, Redis caching layers, web serving architectures, application backends, and continuous integration runners requiring fast local scratch disks.
